== Biography ==
'''Agnes Glasgow''' was a lawful child of [[Glasgow-4152|John Glasgow]], a sailor in Saltcoats
within Ardrossan parish. She and [[Glasgow-4153|Katherine Glasgow]] were named in their
father's testament dative and inventory when his estate came before Glasgow
Commissary Court in April 1637. Their father had died in December 1636.<ref name="JohnTestament">National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court,
testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow, sailor in Saltcoats, NRS
CC9/7/27, register pp. 478–480; death in December 1636 and court proceedings in
April 1637; original register re-read September 2026; locate by reference
through the [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills
Scotland's People wills search].</ref>

The proceeding calls Agnes and Katherine the lawful children of the deceased,
their father. It names '''Isobell Gray''' as John's widow and records that she
gave up the inventory on the children's behalf. This proves Agnes's father and
Isobell's marriage to him, but does not expressly call Isobell Agnes's
mother.<ref name="JohnTestament" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Saltcoats family: selected uncertain earlier father ===

Select John [[Glasgow-3193]], the recorded son at Corsankell in 1571 and probable Kilwinning tenant of 1559–60, as the Saltcoats sailor John [[Glasgow-4152]]’s uncertain working father. Saltcoats in Ardrossan adjoins the Stevenston–Kilwinning coastal parish cluster where this earlier Glasgow family is documented. A later-sixteenth-century son of the earlier adult could have been a working sailor and father of two daughters by 1636. The choice gives the Saltcoats household a provisional place in an existing local John line, using geography and a feasible generation. It is a low-confidence selection, not a named parent clause or an identification of the two Johns.

No source names the sailor’s parents or age. His former c.1600 birth was an unsupported creation estimate; it is not replaced by an invented older birth to fit this hypothesis. If a birth near 1600 is eventually established, the earlier John would have been an older father, and a grandson or more distant collateral placement could be more natural. Same given name is weak support and does not distinguish this candidate securely from [[Glasgow-3921|James Glasgow younger]], another member of the local family, or an unrecorded father. The sailor could belong elsewhere in that family or to another branch. The 1559–60 Kilwinning attribution to the Corsankell John is itself probable, although the 1571 Corsankell family is directly recorded. The same-person alternative is less economical: an adult in 1559 would have been about 95 or older at the sailor’s death in 1636, assuming adulthood at eighteen. That is an illustrative age comparison, not a proved exclusion. The father-versus-grandfather degree remains open. No mother is assigned to the sailor or to his daughters; Agnes Wilson’s joint tenancy does not make her his mother, and Isobell Gray’s widowhood does not prove her maternity. The girls’ already-proved father links remain proved. No identity merge, new original inspection, live WikiTree save or confidence upgrade is made. <ref>National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/27, testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow, sailor in Saltcoats, register pp.478–480, April 1637; death December 1636; original reviewed September 2026; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills record search]. NRS [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD39%2F5%2F59 GD39/5/59], 9 February 1571, James Glasgow elder and sons James and John at Corsankell. Margaret H. B. Sanderson, People of Sixteenth Century Ayrshire, [https://aanhs.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/people-of-ayrshire.pdf#page=38 p.333], Kilwinning teind list, 1559–60. No record names the sailor’s father.</ref>


The testament does not state Agnes's age, birthplace, marriage or death.
Saltcoats is an uncertain creation-field birthplace inferred from her father's
residence, not a stated fact. The document's use of ''bairn'' proves a
parent-child relationship; it does not by itself establish that Agnes was a
young child in 1637.

[[Glasgow-1030]] has been excluded as the present identity of her father: his
documented Glasgow-burgh household has no Saltcoats, sailor, Isobell Gray,
Katherine or Agnes bridge. The distinct Saltcoats father is [[Glasgow-4152]]. His already-confident attachment was verified on 28 September 2026. No mother should be attached
merely because Isobell Gray was John's widow and acted for the children.

A possible identification concerns Agnes Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Agnes Glasgow and James Swan on 12 May 1666 at Kirknewton and East Calder.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 690/10 / 55; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Agnes Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Agnas Glasgow and William Anderson on 5 July 1666 at Longformacus.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 750/10 / 79; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Agnes Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Agnes Glasgow and Patrik Paul on 8 July 1670 at Kirknewton and East Calder.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 690/10 / 64; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.

The banns/marriage index records Agnes Glasgow and William Thomsone on 15 December 1681 at Carstairs.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 633/10 / 66; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected.
